note: The live public schema holds 44 relations: 42 base tables and 2 VIEWS. Per the coordinator ruling the views are marked DERIVED. build_manifest.py enforces this mechanically: a relation with kind 'v' must use disposition_class 'derived-view', and every one of its columns must be 'derived-retirement'. A view carries no rows of its own, so nothing here can be migrated, archived or left unresolved - the only real question is whether each column's BASE fact is dispositioned somewhere else, and that is what the notes record.

user_games_with_catalog.role: The application's read model: user_games joined to catalog_games, plus quarantine flags.
user_games_with_catalog.summary: DERIVED. Not migrated. Rebuilt in v2 from app.library_games, app.game_state, app.game_activity, catalog.games, catalog.game_metadata and catalog.game_features.
user_games_with_catalog.target: rebuilt as a v2 read model; no rows are migrated
evidence: readiness 2 (the two views need an explicit derived line so a coverage assertion can be written mechanically)
readiness 2.1 (the live view still publishes `rating` and `priority`, so the view body was REBUILT REMOTELY and differs from supabase/migrations/20260901193000_share_a_family_library.sql:289)
readiness 10 probe 4 (live routine and view definitions must be exported before mirroring legacy logic)
open_decisions: D-VIEW-1 OPEN (source value): the live view body differs from the repository migration - it publishes rating, priority, title, genre, store and steam_appid as TEXT, columns that no longer exist on live user_games. That the repository definition can be stale is settled; what the LIVE definition actually is can only be read from the source, so probe P04 must export it before any v2 read model mirrors it: snapshot check S-VIEW-DEFS.

id.note: From user_games.id, which is dispositioned there (becomes migration.library_row_map).

title.note: From catalog_games.name, dispositioned there as catalog.games.title.

genre.note: A scalar projection of catalog_games.genres (text[]). The array is preserved as catalog.game_metadata.genres; this single-value flattening is a presentation choice.

store.note: A literal or derived store label. VaultShuffle is Steam-only, so this is a constant in practice and carries no base fact.

ownership.note: From user_games.ownership, which is itself unresolved (D-LIB-3).

status.note: From user_games.status, retired at source as derived (readiness 8.4).

rating.note: readiness 2.1: `rating` NO LONGER EXISTS on live user_games, yet the view still publishes it, so the view body was rebuilt remotely. The base column is retired; the inspection is complete.

hours_played.note: From user_games.hours_played, whose disposition is unresolved pending probe P05.

completion_percentage.note: From user_games.completion_percentage, archived at source as derived evidence.

priority.note: readiness 2.1: `priority` NO LONGER EXISTS on live user_games. Same rebuilt-view evidence as `rating`.

date_added.note: From user_games.date_added. TEXT in DD/MM/YYYY; archived raw at source and NEVER parsed.

steam_appid.note: Published as TEXT here while the base column catalog_steam_appid is BIGINT. A transform reading the view rather than the table would inherit a text appid; this is why the view is not a migration source.

slept_at.note: Retired view projection. Current Blacklist membership is exposed by user_games.status='Blacklisted'; the obsolete timestamp is intentionally absent.

main_extras_minutes.note: From catalog_games.main_extras_minutes, which is unresolved (no v2 destination).

duration_confidence.note: From catalog_games.duration_confidence, unresolved at source (ordinal versus numeric, readiness 4.5).

is_quarantined.note: Computed from the presence of a catalog_game_quarantine row. Recomputable wherever quarantine survives under D-CAT-9.

catalog_steam_appid.note: From user_games.catalog_steam_appid, the BIGINT the text `steam_appid` above is projected from.

price_currency.note: From catalog_games.price_currency, unresolved at source (needs catalog.offer_prices).

steam_tags.note: From catalog_games.tags (jsonb), preserved at source as catalog.game_metadata.weighted_tags.

platform_windows.note: From catalog_games.platform_windows, unresolved at source (no v2 column).

platform_mac.note: From catalog_games.platform_mac, unresolved at source (no v2 column).

platform_linux.note: From catalog_games.platform_linux, transformed at source into the linux_compatibility tri-state.

deck_compatibility.note: From catalog_games.deck_compatibility, unresolved at source (four-way versus tri-state, readiness 4.4).

review_positive.note: From catalog_games.review_positive. The view publishing all three counts confirms the read model needs the triple, not just a score.

review_total.note: From catalog_games.review_total, the denominator of the displayed rating.

release_date.note: From catalog_games.release_date, unresolved at source (no v2 column). A CIVIL DATE.

recency_source.note: From user_games.recency_source (TEXT here, unlike the smallint on the stale user_game_state child).

observed_playtime_minutes.note: From user_games.observed_playtime_minutes, the exact-minutes column preserved at source.

steam_categories.note: From catalog_games.categories (text[]), transformed at source into catalog.game_metadata.categories jsonb.

access_source.note: From user_games.access_source, transformed at source into which relation holds the row.

catalog_duration_review_queue.role: Operator work list of catalogue durations awaiting human review.
catalog_duration_review_queue.summary: DERIVED. Not migrated. Rebuilt in v2 from whatever relations D-CAT-9 and D-DUR-1 create, since every base column belongs to catalog_games or catalog_duration_reviews.
catalog_duration_review_queue.target: rebuilt as a v2 operator read model; no rows are migrated
evidence: readiness 10 probe 4 (export live view definitions before mirroring legacy logic)

duration_status.note: From catalog_games.duration_status; the column that selects rows INTO this queue, and unresolved at source.

users_that_imported.note: From catalog_games.users_that_imported; the demand signal that PRIORITISES the queue. Retired at source as recomputable from app.library_games.

reviewed_at.note: From catalog_duration_reviews.reviewed_at; null means not yet reviewed, which is what puts a row in the queue.

settled_decisions: D-VIEW-2 SETTLED: the queue is rebuildable, because D-CAT-9 is settled (catalog.review_decisions exists) and the catalog_games duration columns are preserved on catalog.game_features. The operator review workflow therefore has a queue in v2 and manual duration decisions have a home.
